focus: D3 Traceability + D4 Maintainability - spec claims sweep, deep-loop YAML convergence machinery, Pi edit_lines section, docs

findingDetails.title: Confirm-mode review workflow never consumes stop_policy so max-iterations can stop before the ceiling
findingDetails.evidence: Both review YAMLs document 'max-iterations treats convergence as telemetry until the hard iteration ceiling' at line 38, but only deep-review-auto.yaml implements it (:624 ':646'); confirm extracts stop_policy (:569) and stores it (:433,:447) while step_check_convergence promotes all-dimensions-clean (:627) and composite convergence to a STOP candidate with no max-iterations guard. Research relies on effective_min_iterations (auto :729, confirm :677), which review does not define. Alternative reading: confirm mode delegates the guard to the operator. Scope note: adjacent to the changed step_convergence_report hunk, not inside it.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add the auto-mode telemetry clause to confirm, or document the confirm-mode difference at line 38.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Statement-level diff of step_check_convergence across the four YAMLs; grep for stop_policy, max-iterations, telemetry and effective_min_iterations in all four; ledger scope shapes cross-checked against deep-review-ledger-schema.vitest.ts

noveltyJustification: Traceability sweep found no unmet manifest-visible requirement across phases 002-005; the phase 5 fan-out close, edit_lines short-count refusal, moved-line refusal and dedup isolation changes are all pinned by tests.
